title: Installer: add preflight checks for VPC networking prerequisites (endpoints/DNS/egress) aligned with Terraform module defaults
creator: Irene Choi
description:
Context
- We’re publishing alpha Terraform modules for AWS VPC private deployments with Redwood-validated defaults (endpoints, private DNS, logging, etc.). The installer currently fails late when networking prerequisites are missing/misconfigured (e.g., can’t pull images; intermittent DNS).
- We have at least one recurring failure mode from pilots: missing ECR interface endpoints and/or private DNS disabled, causing image pulls to fail after cluster bring-up starts.

Goal
Add installer preflight checks that validate the network prerequisites expected by the Terraform modules, with clear error/warn messaging and links to the deployment guide.

Scope (alpha)
- Detect likely missing/misconfigured VPC endpoints required for a fully-private deployment flow.
- Validate VPC-level DNS settings and endpoint private DNS behavior.
- Produce actionable remediation instructions that map to the terraform module inputs/README.
- Roll out as warn-first (non-breaking) with an opt-in strict mode; coordinate with Solutions Eng + Support.

Non-goals
- Full connectivity validation (VPN/DX reachability tests) beyond placeholder checks.
- Generic customer network audits; keep checks constrained to what the installer can reliably infer via AWS APIs and simple runtime probes.

Proposed checks (installer preflight)
1) VPC DNS settings
- Verify VPC has enableDnsSupport=true and enableDnsHostnames=true.
- If false: hard error in strict mode; warn in default mode.

2) Required VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink / Gateway)
For private EKS + private image pulls, we should at minimum flag the following when absent in the target VPC:
- Interface endpoints: com.amazonaws.${region}.ecr.api, com.amazonaws.${region}.ecr.dkr, com.amazonaws.${region}.logs, com.amazonaws.${region}.sts
- Gateway endpoint: com.amazonaws.${region}.s3
Notes:
- We should also consider warning on missing: ec2, elasticloadbalancing, autoscaling, kms (depending on installer behavior + control plane interactions).
- Do not hardcode “must have all endpoints” unless strict mode is enabled; customers may rely on NAT/proxy egress.

3) Endpoint private DNS
- If an interface endpoint exists but PrivateDnsEnabled=false, warn that it often causes failures (ECR is the most sensitive).
- For ECR: recommend enabling private DNS on ecr.api/ecr.dkr endpoints or explicitly configuring DNS/proxy per guide.

4) Egress posture heuristics
- If required endpoints are missing, attempt a lightweight probe from installer runtime:
  - DNS resolve test for api.ecr.${region}.amazonaws.com and ${account}.dkr.ecr.${region}.amazonaws.com (don’t require account id; resolve base hostnames).
  - Optional HTTPS reachability check with short timeout (warn-only). Avoid long hangs.
- Messaging should be explicit: either configure endpoints (recommended) OR ensure NAT/proxy egress + DNS works.

5) Output expectations alignment
- If installer is provided VPC/subnet IDs (or can discover from cluster config), print the exact identifiers used to evaluate endpoints so Support can reproduce quickly.

Acceptance criteria
- Installer prints a “Network prerequisites” section during preflight with:
  - VPC DNS settings status
  - Endpoint presence/absence table (at least ECR/S3/STS/Logs)
  - Endpoint private DNS status (where applicable)
  - Clear remediation steps and links
- Default behavior: warnings only (no new hard failures) for alpha rollout.
- Strict mode: `--strict-network-preflight` (or env var) converts the most common fatal issues into errors:
  - Missing both (a) ECR endpoints and (b) proven egress (we can’t reliably prove egress; so strict mode should error only on missing endpoints + VPC DNS disabled, and otherwise remain warn-only).
  - VPC DNS support/hostnames disabled => error.
- Unit tests for parsing endpoint inventory and message rendering.
- One integration test run in a sandbox VPC with endpoints disabled to ensure messages are emitted (can be in nightly suite if too expensive).

References / linked work
- Support signal: SUP-28411 “installer fails pulling images (missing ECR endpoints)”
- Support signal: SUP-28458 “intermittent DNS resolution in private subnets”
- Related terraform work: vpc-endpoints module + DNS options (ENG-4844)
- Target PR (installer): redwood-private-installer PR-19110 “Detect VPC endpoints and warn on missing ECR”
- Follow-up docs PR: redwood-private-installer PR-19144 “Installer docs for terraform module integration”

Implementation notes
- Use AWS APIs (DescribeVpcs, DescribeVpcEndpoints) scoped to VPC ID.
- Endpoint discovery should handle multiple endpoints per service (multi-subnet) and accept “present if any endpoint exists for service” but warn if endpoint is not in the expected subnets/security groups only if we can check reliably.
- Keep endpoint list centralized and versioned (match module defaults). Add comment pointing to the confluence reference architecture to update list when defaults change.

Rollout checklist
- [ ] Land PR-19110 behind warn-only defaults
- [ ] Add doc section in installer docs + link to terraform deployment guide
- [ ] Notify Solutions Eng (Markus Klein / Colin O’Donnell) of new preflight output and how to interpret warnings during pilots
- [ ] Update Support runbook: “Missing ECR endpoints” troubleshooting now starts with preflight output
- [ ] During alpha: collect warning frequency + top missing endpoints to refine module defaults and strict-mode policy

Open questions
- Should we include CloudWatch Logs endpoint as “recommended” vs “required”? (Security prefers on by default; some customers send logs elsewhere.)
- Do we want to error if BOTH (a) no S3 gateway endpoint and (b) no NAT detected? NAT detection isn’t reliable from installer; keep warn-only for alpha.
comments: 2025-06-21 (Nina Petrova): Agreed on starting with ECR/S3/STS/Logs + VPC DNS flags. We’ve seen ECR private DNS off even when endpoints exist; adding explicit check + message will save hours in pilots. Will keep strict mode minimal to avoid breaking customers using NAT/proxy egress.

2025-06-24 (Victor Alvarez): Endpoint presence check is straightforward via DescribeVpcEndpoints filtered by vpc-id + service-name. Suggest we print the resolved region + vpc-id + list of endpoint IDs found for troubleshooting. For private DNS: field is PrivateDnsEnabled on the endpoint object for interface endpoints.

2025-06-25 (Sean Gallagher): Please keep probes time-bounded; we had installer preflight hang reports in other areas. Recommend 1s DNS, 2s HTTPS max; warn-only. Add a single summary line at end: PASS / WARN / FAIL (strict mode only).

2025-06-27 (Marcus Lin): From Security POV: default should strongly recommend endpoints over NAT egress for regulated customers. Messaging should avoid implying NAT is required; instead say NAT/proxy is an alternative but must be customer-managed and audited. Add link to logging + least-privilege docs where relevant.

2025-07-02 (Nina Petrova): Implemented in PR-19110. Default is WARN. Added `--strict-network-preflight` which errors only on VPC DNS settings disabled. Missing endpoints remain WARN (even in strict) until we have better signal. Added clear remediation: ‘enable interface endpoints for ecr.api/ecr.dkr with private DNS enabled’ + ‘add S3 gateway endpoint’ + link to terraform module docs.

2025-07-07 (Rafael Mendes): Tested against sandbox VPC with no endpoints: preflight output is readable and correctly calls out ECR + S3 + STS. Verified VPC DNS disabled case errors in strict mode only. Good to ship for alpha; request follow-up to export a machine-readable JSON blob for support tooling (out of scope).
